comparisons.interpretation: West supports diminishing reliance on a policing-centered model while greatly increasing social services. Krebs explicitly supports reducing the NYPD budget, removing police from roles better handled by other responders, and reinvesting funds. These are related public-safety strategies, but West’s excerpt does not itself commit to a specific budget cut; no opposition is inferred.

West emphasizes moving away from policing-centered community safety and increasing social services. Hanif specifies defunding the NYPD budget by at least $3 billion. West’s excerpt does not establish a numerical budget position, so this is a difference in emphasis and specificity, not opposition.

Both support climate action. Canning frames climate protection as a central campaign priority, while Hoyle specifies a 100% clean-electricity standard. This is a difference in specificity and emphasis; neither excerpt establishes opposition to the other’s approach.

Both address housing supply and affordability. Avilés emphasizes public investment, preservation, and tenant protections; Ye emphasizes developer incentives. Neither excerpt establishes opposition to the other mechanism.
